evidence.title: Why Workers Binge-Watch: Insights from the Theory of Planned Behavior and Social Exchange Theory
evidence.author: Aspary, Octaviniant; Firliani, Alifia; Ilham, Muhammad
excerpts: Binge watching has become a widespread habit in the digital age, significantly impacting various aspects of life, including work productivity and social interactions.
Vast evidence suggests significant implications to binge watching, including lower productivity, and worse mental health and overall wellbeing.
This study aims to analyze binge watching behavior among workers using the Planned Behavior Theory and Social Exchange Theory as the conceptual framework.
The research adopts a quantitative approach, utilizing Google Sheets and SmartPLS for data analysis.

The sample, selected using a snowball sampling technique, consists of 100 respondents who are of productive age, residing in Jabodetabek (Jakarta, Bogor, Depok, Tangerang, Bekasi) Indonesia Area, and engaged in employment or business activities.
The analysis revealed that attitude and perceived behavioral control significantly influence the intention to binge-watch, while subjective norms show a weaker association.
Intention strongly predicts actual binge-watching behavior among workers, supporting the applicability of the Theory of Planned Behavior in this context.
Reward-cost evaluation, derived from Social Exchange Theory, demonstrates a direct positive effect on binge-watching behavior but not on intention.
These results illustrate how cognitive and motivational factors collectively shape binge-watching habits within the working population.
Future studies are encouraged to expand this model across diverse occupational and cultural contexts and to explore the long-term impacts of binge-watching on work-life balance and mental health.

evidence.title: 13 Reasons Why
excerpts: 13 Reasons Why (also stylized as TH1RTEEN R3ASONS WHY) is an American teen drama television series based on the 2007 novel Thirteen Reasons Why by author Jay Asher.
Developed for Netflix by Brian Yorkey and with Selena Gomez serving as an executive producer, the series stars Dylan Minnette and Katherine Langford alongside an ensemble cast.
The series follows the students of the fictional Liberty High School and the wide range of social issues affecting modern youth.
The show originally revolved around Clay Jensen (Minnette) and the aftermath of the suicide of fellow student Hannah Baker (Langford).
Before her death, she leaves behind a box of cassette tapes in which she details the reasons why she chose to kill herself as well as the people she believes are responsible for her death.
It became the second most watched series on Netflix at the time of its release.
Netflix renewed 13 Reasons Why for a second season due to the success of the initial 13 episodes; the second season was released on May 18, 2018.
A third season was released on August 23, 2019; that same month, the series was renewed for a fourth and final season, which was released on June 5, 2020.

The first season received positive reviews from critics and audiences, who praised its themes, emotional weight, subject matter, character development and acting, particularly the performances of Minnette and Langford.
Subsequently, it prompted concerns from mental health professionals due to its graphic depiction of issues such as suicide, sexual assault, and bullying, along with other mature content.
The later three seasons were met with a negative critical response.

Coinciding with the release of the second season, Netflix released a video with the cast that cautioned viewers about some of the topics covered in the show and provided a support website with crisis numbers for people affected by depression, anxiety, and other mental health issues.

evidence.title: Hate-watching
excerpts: Hate-watching is the activity of consuming media, usually a television show or a film with the intention of acquiring amusement from the mockery of its content or subject.
Closely related to anti-fan behaviours, viewers who partake in hate-watching derive pleasure and entertainment from a show's absurdities or failures.
The act of hate-watching is premised on the audience engaging with media through a satirical lens.

evidence.title: Golden Age of Television (2000s–2023)
excerpts: In the United States, there have been periods of time described as having such a number of high quality (or "prestige"), internationally acclaimed television programs, that they can be regarded as the Golden Age of Television.
One such period stretched roughly from 2000 to 2023, with a subset of this era also known as Peak TV or the Prestige TV era.
Named in reference to the original Golden Age of Television of the 1950s, more recent periods have also been referred to as the "New", "Second", or "Third Golden Age of Television".
The various names reflect disagreement over whether shows of the 1980s and early-mid 1990s belong to a since-concluded golden era or to the current one.

The contemporary period is generally identified as beginning in 1999 with The Sopranos, with debate as to whether the age ended (or "peaked") in the mid-late 2010s or early 2020s (to the point of calling its replacement "Trough TV"), or remains ongoing.

evidence.title: Dallas Jenkins
excerpts: Dallas Jenkins (born July 25, 1975) is an American film and television director, writer and producer.
He is best known as the creator, director, co-writer and executive producer of The Chosen, the first multi-season series about the life of Jesus of Nazareth.
